title: Month control gave no clear change in floral pigment trends in six herbarium samples from 1941 to 2017
abstract: We tested whether collection-season control changed time trends in flower UV pigmentation. Six samples used 1,230 herbarium specimens from Australia, Eurasia and North America in 1941-1985 and 1986-2017. We compared species and location models with models that added species-specific month controls. The paired trend changes ranged from -0.99 to +2.07 percentage points per decade. All six species-cluster intervals included zero after a six-test correction. Month control retained 66-86% of residual time variation. Equal-species weights changed one contrast sign. The results do not establish that collection season is harmless or that biological trends are absent. Nonrandom collection, sparse month cells, shared source records and uncertain species-cluster inference limit the test. The package gives code, source hashes, aggregate results, a figure and independent numerical checks. The external workbook stays outside the bundle.

display.caption: Time slopes with and without species-specific month controls in six region-period samples. Units are percentage points of UV-absorbing petal area per decade. Intervals use a t reference with species clusters and a six-test Bonferroni multiplier. Paired contrast intervals are in the text and results table.
